title: Employer Benefit Charging: Disputed Charge Amount in a Separation Response
content:
Under Employer Benefit Charging, the disputed charge amount is the money a separation response puts in dispute, worked out on the day the response is received.

> The disputed charge amount is the financing basis of the charges the response counts, less the charges it leaves out, never below zero, times the response class share and times the answer window share, rounded to the cent.

The response counts no charge, the financing basis is nothing and no charge is left out; the response class share is zero (0.00), the value an Extended Benefits state-share position receives because its relief follows the determination on the regular claim; and the answer window share is three quarters (0.75), the value of a late answer once a payment has been charged while it was overdue.

## Structure of the figure

- The charges left out are subtracted from the financing basis first; a negative difference is taken as zero.
- That difference is multiplied by the response class share and by the answer window share.
- The product is rounded to the cent once, at the end.

## Worked example (hypothetical)

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Charges the response counts | none |
| Financing basis | $0.00 |
| Charges left out | $0.00 |
| Basis less charges left out, not below zero | $0.00 |
| Times the response class share (0.00) and the answer window share (0.75) | $0.00 |
| Disputed charge amount, rounded to the cent | $0.00 |
